Meeting header: 2026-08-09 15:30 PST (72 minutes) | Recording ID: ff_20260809_stargaze_001
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Vasquez (Redwood CSM), Lina Patel (Redwood SE); Priya Malhotra (CTO), Ben Gomez (Cloud Architect), Ruth Chang (Security Lead), Ethan Park (DevOps), Sam Lee (Product)

Auto-generated summary (auto): Quick implementation kickoff for Stargaze Systems to onboard Redwood Private (VPC) with staging and production runbooks. Key topics: network connectivity, SSO, SOC2/audit artifacts, pilot scope and success metrics (latency, cost), initial performance baseline and sample prompts. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics: network and VPC peering; hosted vs dedicated vs private; SSO/SAML and SCIM; SOC 2 / audit evidence; staging checklist and sample prompts; rollback/fallback plan; timeline for pilot (2-3 weeks).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone. thanks for joining, we— we are recording. quick intro from our side, i'm maya, i'll be your ae, with omar and lina. ok, priya?
[00:08] Priya Malhotra: hi yep, priya here. thanks for doing this. we are looking to integrate redwood for our customer support LLM features, must keep PII off platform and we have a strict latency requirement for chat ops.
[00:22] Ben Gomez: ben here— cloud architect. we'll handle networking. main constraint is we are multi-region and prefer VPC mode with dedicated capacity for promopeak-days.
[00:33] Ruth Chang: ruth — security. our compliance team wants SOC2 evidence, KMS integration and SAML for SSO. also audit log retention for 13 months.
[00:44] Ethan Park: ethan, devops. interested in rollout cadence: staging -> canary -> prod and automatic fallback.
[00:50] Maya Chen: great. quick agenda: 1) clarify success criteria & timeline 2) network/connectivity and hosting mode 3) auth and security controls 4) staging runbook and pilot scope 5) next steps. sound good?
[00:59] Priya Malhotra: yep. one note — cost is sensitive, we'd like an idea of per-req costing so product can model monthly spend.
[01:07] Omar Vasquez: totally, we'll send an initial cost model based on your QPS. lina will capture baseline perf numbers on our side.

[01:15] Lina Patel: hi all. quick background: redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC deployments. for your PII requirements, private VPC with customer-managed KMS is typically recommended. there are tradeoffs on latency/cost vs hosted.
[01:33] Ben Gomez: can you walk us through the VPC flow — egress, peering, NAT, ingress? we've got a few hops (ap-southeast and us-west).
[01:40] Lina Patel: yes. for private we do a secure peering (or aws private link) from your VPC into the redwood private runtime. best practice is to terminate the KV-cache and serving nodes in the redwood infra but keep control plane in the public region. sometimes customers want full on-prem, that’s also possible but longer lead time.

[01:58] Ruth Chang: when you say KMS, is that customer-managed key only, or do you have bring-your-own-HSM options? our legal wants HSM-backed key material for certain workloads.
[02:07] Lina Patel: we support customer-managed keys via KMS; HSM-on-prem integrations are available as an enterprise add-on — need a security review and lead time. i'll flag that as a separate security path.

[02:18] Priya Malhotra: timeline — ideally pilot in two weeks, production in 6 weeks. is that plausible?
[02:25] Maya Chen: pilot in two weeks is aggressive but doable if we have sample prompts and network access this week. prod in six weeks — we'll map sprints and dependencies.
[02:34] Ethan Park: what about throughput? expected concurrency for chat is about 40 qps during peak but average 6 qps. token lengths vary — avg 120 tokens.
[02:44] Lina Patel: good, that helps. for 40 qps with 120 tokens we’ll recommend an x-large dedicated profile, or a VPC private with auto scale policy. we can show cost tradeoffs in the spreadsheet.

[02:55] Ben Gomez: do you have benchmarking runbooks? we'd like to run an initial perf test inside our staging VPC against the redwood runtime.
[03:02] Lina Patel: yes, we have a perf harness (link: https://redwood.internal/perf-harness — placeholder) and a spreadsheet for token accounting. we'll send a sample JMeter and k6 config.

[03:15] Sam Lee: product question — we have a reranking stage after generation, can redwood host both generation + embeddings to reduce network hops?
[03:23] Lina Patel: absolutely. colocating embedding and generation on the same model variant or same runtime reduces latency. we'll recommend a combined topology for your path if you want rerank inline.

[03:34] Priya Malhotra: about data retention: some transcripts need to be kept internally for 13 months, others are ephemeral. can we configure retention per-route?
[03:42] Omar Vasquez: yes per-route retention policies are configurable in the console. for private deployments, retention and logs remain in-customer or routed to a customer S3 with lifecycle rules.

[03:52] Ruth Chang: SSO specifics — we use Okta, need SCIM provisioning and role-based access controls. can you support SCIM groups and attribute mapping?
[03:59] Lina Patel: we support SAML SSO + SCIM. SCIM group mapping and custom attributes are supported; we'll provide the attribute mapping doc and sample claim set.

[04:10] Ben Gomez: what about network egress costs? if we route embeddings back and forth, costs can balloon. any caching to reduce token spend?
[04:18] Lina Patel: we have prefix caching and KV cache options. caching can reduce tokens for repeated prompts significantly, we can show examples from similar customers. also batching helps but affects latency.

[04:29] Ethan Park: can you explain fallback behavior — say if dedicated capacity is exhausted? we want graceful degradation to a cheaper model not fail open.
[04:36] Lina Patel: routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants; we support automatic fallback to a lower-cost region or model tier with a circuit-breaker policy and rate-limited downgrade to protect latency SLOs.

[04:48] Priya Malhotra: security demo — can we get a short walkthrough of audit logs and how they appear?
[04:52] Omar Vasquez: sure, Lina can show screenshots in follow-up; for today i'll attach our SOC2 kit and audit log sample.

[05:00] Maya Chen: ok let's do a quick intake checklist — who owns what so we can hit pilot in 2 weeks.
[05:06] Priya Malhotra: priya to own product acceptance criteria and user flows.
[05:09] Ben Gomez: ben to do networking and provide IP ranges, peering preference (peering vs PrivateLink), and expected QPS by 8/12.
[05:16] Ruth Chang: ruth will provide SOC2 scope and compliance contacts by next friday.
[05:20] Ethan Park: ethan will prepare staging k8s ingress and test service to run perf tests.
[05:25] Maya Chen: redwood side — we will prepare runbook, perf harness, SSO guide, and initial cost model. lina will own the staging integration checklist.
[05:33] Sam Lee: question on pricing — do you have committed commit discounts for a 12-month reserved pool?
[05:38] Maya Chen: yes we offer reserved capacity pricing; i'll send the options and a simple TCO comparison for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[05:45] Priya Malhotra: any blockers for starting?
[05:48] Lina Patel: main blockers would be network access (peering) and sample prompts plus QPS numbers. SAML test user helps accelerate SSO.
[05:56] Ben Gomez: noted — i'll prod infra and get IP ranges in the next 48 hours.
[06:01] Ruth Chang: also note legal is picky about egress to third-party storage. we may need to route logs to our S3.
[06:07] Omar Vasquez: that's supported — for private deployments we can configure logs to ship to your bucket with encryption.
[06:13] Priya Malhotra: great. one last item — can you confirm incident escalation path and contact for after-hours?
[06:18] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include on-call contacts and SLA escalation matrix in the runbook.
[06:23] Lina Patel: i'll also include a quick troubleshooting playbook for the most common failures (auth, peering, certificate rotation).
[06:30] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and who does what — (recap). we'll aim to send the onboarding packet today and schedule the VPC deep-dive for wednesday 8/12 at 10am PT.
[06:44] Priya Malhotra: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:47] Ben Gomez: thanks. bye.
[06:49] Ruth Chang: bye.
[06:50] Recording ended.
